This is the first criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 filed on behalf of the appellant for grant of bail.

The appellant is in custody since 20.1.2023 in connection with Crime No.18/2023 registered at Police Station "

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, appellant and prosecutrix both resides in same village.

3-4 months prior to lodging the report, while prosecutrix was crossing the field of appellant, then appellant caught her and committed rape upon her and threatened her that if she discloses the incident to anyone then he will kill her family.

Thereafter on 26.12.2022 at about 11 pm when the prosecutrix went to Khargone the appellant reached there and told her for contracting marriage with him and also threatened that if she denies, he will defame her.
Thereafter the appellant took her to Gujarat kept her in a hut and committed rape upon her several times.
On 12.1.2023 she anyhow fled away from there and returned to her home and lodged the FIR.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the appellant.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.

He is in custody since 20.1.2023,
the prosecutrix is a 24 years old major and married lady having two children, she was the consenting party and not happy with her husband.
The MLC report has not supported the case of prosecution, the prosecutrix on her own accord went to Gujarat and lived with the appellant, FIR is about 3-4 months belated.
The appellant is a young person of 22 years of age and permanent resident of District Khargone, final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the criminal appeal and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutirx has supported the FIR version in her statement given under section 164 Cr.P.C.
Counsel for objector also opposes the appeal and prays for its rejection.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence, and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix is a 24 years old major and married lady, FIR is 3-4 months belated, MLC report has not supported the case of prosecution, investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed, but final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time, I deem it proper to release the appellant on bail.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

It is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Shivam vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153665672/
